newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Anglo says Mali mine pours first gold.
newsitem.headline: Anglo says Mali mine pours first gold.

text.p: South Africa's Anglo American Corp said on Monday that its Sadiola Hill gold mine in the West African country of Mali had completed its first gold pour on December 20.

The pour means the plant's first processing line has been successfully started up. The line is set to reach full capacity by the end of February with both modules of the plant operating fully by the end of May.
Sadiola's first module was commissioned in early November and started up using a process of progression from waste ore to low grade gold ore.
At full capacity the plant will produce about one tonne of gold per month with the available oxide ore reserves containing 140 tonnes of gold.
The construction of the treatment plant and mine village was completed on schedule fifteen months after the start of on-site construction.

Anglo owns 38 percent of the investment vehicle in control of the mine, Societe d'Exploration des Mines d'Or de Sadiola. The other partners are Canada's IAMGOLD with 38 percent and the International Finance Corp with six percent.
